# Yarrow · 三易

> I Ching and BaZi readings by three classical masters, paid in USDC on Arc mainnet. Every I Ching cast can be recomputed from Arc block hashes.

- Site: https://yarrow-six.vercel.app
- Source: https://github.com/fangTiger/yarrow
- Price: 0.05 USDC per reading on Arc mainnet (chain ID 5042). Gas on Arc is also paid in USDC.
- Trust model: the server only reads Arc. It holds no private keys and never moves funds. You pay on-chain yourself, then claim the reading with your transaction hash. Each payment opens exactly one reading.

## How an agent buys a reading

1. **Discover the price.** POST your request to `/api/readings` without `feeProof`. A valid request returns **HTTP 402** with:
   `{"code": "payment-proof-required", "payment": {"chainId": 5042, "token": "0x3600000000000000000000000000000000000000", "recipient": "0x…", "amountUsdc6": "50000"}}`
   An invalid request returns 400 before any payment is asked for, so you never pay for a request that can't run. `GET /api/payment` returns the same `payment` object.
2. **Pay.** Transfer exactly `amountUsdc6` (6 decimals: 50000 = 0.05 USDC) of `token` to `recipient` on Arc, using the ERC-20 `transfer` function. Wait for the receipt.
3. **Claim.** POST the same request again with `"feeProof": {"payer": "<your address>", "transactionHash": "<0x… tx hash>"}`. The response is the reading, including its `id`. If the claim fails before the payment is accepted (for example, a validation error), the payment stays unused and you can retry with it.
4. **Poll.** `GET /api/readings/{id}` until `status` is `"done"`. Readings usually take 30 to 120 seconds. The response has `summary.output` (plain-language conclusion and practical guidance) and `schools` (the three masters' readings).
5. **English (optional).** The readings are written in Chinese. To get English, call `POST /api/readings/{id}/translate` with `{"lang": "en"}`, then `GET /api/readings/{id}?lang=en`. The `translation` field fills in as units finish.
6. **Verify (optional).** For an I Ching reading, take `payment.firstHash` and each `throws[i].blockNumber`, then read the block hash from Arc. Each throw is the lowest three bits of
   `keccak256(encodePacked(string "sanyi-throw-v1", bytes32 paymentTxHash, bytes32 blockHash, string question, uint8 index))`,
   where 1 is the back of a coin and 0 the face. Every cast block must come after the payment block.

Write requests must send `Content-Type: application/json` and `Origin: https://yarrow-six.vercel.app` (a cross-site request guard), with a body of 8 KiB at most.

## Request bodies

- **I Ching question.** Pass `kind` and `subjectKey`. The server's keyword classifier recognizes common English and Chinese wording, but anything it can't place falls back to `peers`, so an explicit `subjectKey` is more reliable.
  `{"kind": "question", "question": "Will my new business partnership work out this year?", "subjectKey": "career"}`
  `subjectKey` is one of `career`, `wealth`, `documents`, `wellbeing`, `illness`, `peers`, `relationship`.
- **BaZi destiny (life luck cycles and character).**
  `{"kind": "destiny", "question": "How will my life unfold, and what is my character like?", "sect": 1, "birth": {"calendar": "solar", "isLeapMonth": false, "year": 1990, "month": 5, "day": 15, "time": {"hour": 14, "minute": 30}, "gender": "female", "timeZone": "America/New_York"}}`
  Use `"time": null` if the birth hour is unknown. `timeZone` is an IANA name and defaults to `Asia/Shanghai`.
- **BaZi fortune.** The same as destiny, with `"kind": "fortune"` and `"horizon"` set to `"today"`, `"month"`, `"year"`, `"next-year"` or `"year:2027"`.
- **Naming.** `{"kind": "naming", "target": "person", "question": "gentle and literary", "surname": "林", "gender": "female", "length": 2, "unborn": false, "birth": {…}}`. For a business name, use `"target": "business"` and a `length` from 2 to 4.

## Example

`scripts/agent-reading.ts` in the repository runs the whole flow with viem: it reads the 402, pays on Arc, claims the reading and polls until it is done.

This is HTTP 402 payment discovery, not the full x402 protocol. Yarrow never submits signed transfers on your behalf, so it needs no keys.
